title: Same Money, Same Rate. Why Is One 4x Bigger? | Money Explained #2
simplified: EXAMPLE only: 1,000 in any currency ($ or ₹), a fixed 10% a year paid once a year, 30 years, no fees, taxes or inflation. Real rates change and are not guaranteed. Left pile = interest paid out each year (only the starting amount earns); right pile = interest left in (annual compounding).

hook_candidates.text: Same money. Same rate. Why is this pile four times bigger?
Both piles earn ten percent. One ends up four times bigger.
You and your twin save the same. Thirty years later, you're four times richer.
Watch this clock run thirty years. Guess which pile wins.
This coin is paying rent to another coin.

parts.text: Why is this pile four times bigger?
Both earn ten percent a year.
This pile spends its interest each year.
Its total climbs in a straight line.
So next year, the interest earns interest too.
For years, the gap stays small.
and each year adds more than the last.
The extra is interest on interest.

sources: Compound interest = interest on the money saved and on the interest earned along the way: 'Compound interest is when you earn interest on the money you've saved and on the interest you earn along the way.' CFPB, 'What is compound interest?', https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-compound-interest-en-1683/ (read 2026-11-28); its worked example: $1,000 at 5% -> $1,050 -> $1,102.50. Investor.gov glossary 'Compounding interest', https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/compounding-interest

Figures (EXAMPLE, own arithmetic, re-checked): 1,000 at 10% a year compounded annually for 30 years = 1,000 x 1.1^30 = 17,449.40. With interest paid out each year: 1,000 + 30 x 100 = 4,000 in total (1,000 kept + 3,000 paid out). Ratio 4.36, 'four times bigger'. Interest-on-interest part = 17,449 - 4,000 = 13,449. Year 11: 2,853 vs 2,100, a gap of 753, small next to the final gap of 13,449 ('for years, the gap stays small'). Yearly addition on the right = 10% of the balance, so each year adds more than the last.
Spoken numbers: 'thirty years' and 'ten percent' (two); '4x' in the hook is the comparison. The 10% rate is a round illustrative number, not a typical or promised return; shown on screen as EXAMPLE.
Finance safety: explains the mechanism only. No product, account, fund or rate is named or recommended.
